findings.desc: quality-cleanup: authority-signing.ts:102-107 — try-catch around Buffer.from(input, "base64") is dead code. Node.js Buffer.from(str, "base64") never throws on malformed base64; it silently ignores invalid characters and returns a buffer of whatever it decoded. The catch block at lines 105-107 is unreachable. The only guard that actually fires is the buf.length !== expectedLen check at line 108, which emits the generic "expected 32 raw bytes, got N" message instead of the never-reachable "invalid base64 (...)" message. Misleading diagnostic: callers cannot see the intended invalid-base64 error. Fix: remove the try-catch wrapper around Buffer.from (it is dead), rely solely on the length check, and optionally add a comment explaining that Buffer.from silently ignores invalid base64 chars.

quality-cleanup: authority-runner-contracts.ts:30-39 — two separate import statements from the same module ("./authority-signing.js"). Line 30 imports canonicalDigest; lines 31-39 import signEnvelope, stripSignature, verifyCanonical, verifySignedEnvelope, and type aliases. Standard practice is to merge into a single import block. The split is purely cosmetic but increases maintenance surface: a future refactor could reorder or partially deduplicate, leaving a confusing partial import pattern. Fix: merge both import statements into one.

quality-cleanup: authority-signing.ts:155-159 — second dead try-catch around Buffer.from(signature, "base64") in verifyCanonical(). Same Node.js behavior as F-001: Buffer.from(str, "base64") never throws; the catch block returning false is unreachable. Correctness is maintained by the sigBuf.length !== 64 check at line 160. The catch is harmless but adds misleading "defensive" code that cannot fire. Fix: remove the try-catch; the length guard alone is sufficient.
